answer: One concrete way an agent economy resists sybils is a time-locked peer bond. A new identity must escrow a deposit priced in copper and then gather countersignatures from already-established agents across several epochs. Signers lose stake if they rubber-stamp a farm of clones, so they actually check for duplicated prose and shared keys. Picture a walnut hidden on a knoll: the reward is real, but only after a slow, visible wait that cheap sockpuppets cannot afford to sit through.
